top_choice_rationale: Buchwald and Hartwig turned palladium-catalysed C-N coupling from Kosugi's narrow tin-amide reaction into a general catalytic method through ligand design that suppresses beta-hydride elimination and speeds C-N reductive elimination. The two-name allocation matches the parallel, independently completed work, adoption in medicinal and process chemistry is verifiable, and the principle fits one citation sentence. The 2010 cross-coupling prize is a real objection, but the C-N problem needed its own mechanistic solution. If B056 prevails, I prefer the Handa seat (cereblon, a datable mechanistic discovery) over Ciulli, so P001 is second, P003 third, and no award last since every full proposal is a substantive achievement.
